title: The postcard run, ii
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
logline: A postcard with no picture. Just her handwriting on both sides. Wood pins it by the corner so both sides show.

panels.composition: The mailbox. WOOD pulling out a card that is blank cardstock, both sides written on. BARNABY.

image.prompt: a young man at a roadside mailbox reading a plain cardstock postcard written on both sides, a small dog beside him, brush-pen black and white

panels.composition: Her handwriting, one side: 'W — No picture this time. I couldn't find one that looked like here. Here doesn't look like anything yet. That's the point of it. — C.'

image.prompt: a panel that is a plain postcard covered in tiny handwritten capitals, ink on cardstock

panels.composition: The other side: a drawing. Hers. A bad, wonderful drawing of a Chicago street with an arrow: ME. And, off the edge, an arrow: YOU, 2,100 MI. She's copied his map.

image.prompt: a panel that is a crude but charming pen drawing of a city street on cardstock with an arrow labeled ME and another arrow pointing off the edge
image.notes: Her version of his 1999 map (#33). Letter ME and YOU, 2,100 MI after.

panels.composition: The corkboard. Wood pinning it by one corner so it hangs free and both sides can be turned. The only card on the board that shows its writing.

characters.pose: pinning a card by one corner

image.prompt: a young man pinning a postcard to a corkboard by a single corner so it hangs free among other cards pinned flat, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen over rough blue pencil; xerox grain; stark spotting; rain in frantic vertical hatching (Arc 1's aesthetic)

notes: She copies his map back to him. The only postcard he pins writing-out.
